Apply a function to a tagged wave and record the process

Source: R/tagApply.R
tagApply.Rd

Runs fun(w, ...) and, if w is a TaggedWave or TaggedWaveMC, appends a record of the call to the processing slot of the result. The record holds the function name, its arguments, the time, the duration and digests of the input and output. Untagged waves are processed without any record being made, so tagApply() can be used safely in code that handles either.

Usage

tagApply(.w, .fun, ..., label = NULL, untag = NA, cl = NULL)

Arguments

.w

A Wave, WaveMC, TaggedWave or TaggedWaveMC object, or a list of such objects.

.fun

A function, or the name of one, taking the wave as its first argument.

...

Further arguments passed to .fun.

label

Optional. A description of the process. Defaults to the name of the function.

untag

Whether to pass .fun an untagged wave (see Details). The default, NA, does so for functions from other packages.

cl

Optional. A cluster, as made by parallel::makeCluster(), used to process a list of waves in parallel. The workers need sonicscrewdriver to be available.

Value

The result of .fun, with the process recorded if .w is tagged.

Details

If fun returns a wave without tags, the origin, metadata and processing of w are carried over to it. The spectrogram_maad_power slot is not carried over, as it no longer matches the signal.

If fun returns something that is not a wave, such as a number or a data frame, there is no tagged object to hold the record. The result is returned with an attribute processing holding the history of w followed by the new record (without an output digest). A NULL result is returned as it is.

Functions from other packages are given an untagged wave. seewave, for example, checks the class of a wave with class(w)[1] == "Wave" and so rejects a TaggedWave. The tags are put back on a wave that is returned, as described above. Functions from this package and functions defined by the user are given the tagged wave unless untag = TRUE.

Only the outermost call makes a record. A function that calls tagApply() itself, as a function of this package may come to, is recorded once when it is passed to tagApply() in turn, under the name and arguments of the outer call rather than twice under both.

The wave and the function are named .w and .fun so that the arguments meant for .fun reach it. R matches a named argument against the arguments named before ... by its first letters as well as in full, so a plain w and fun would swallow anything called f, fu or w - and f is what seewave calls a sampling frequency, which is exactly the sort of call this function is for. label, untag and cl come after ... and so must be named in full, which leaves only a function with an argument of one of those three names beyond reach.

Examples

tw <- tagWave(tuneR::sine(440, duration = 44100, samp.rate = 44100))
tw <- tagApply(tw, tuneR::normalize, unit = "16")
#> Warning: pcm set to TRUE since unit was one of 8, 16, or 24
tw@processing[[1]]$func
#> [1] "tuneR::normalize"

# seewave functions can be used with tagged waves
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
tw <- tagApply(tw, seewave::ffilter, from = 1000, to = 2000, output = "Wave")
} # }
